name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 motor-propelled up to 20 mph. Defined by Idaho Code §49-106 and regulated by §§49-725 through 49-729; HB 500 (2026) added it to the traffic-rights and due-care rules of §§49-714 and 49-615 from July 1, 2026.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and a motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, required since September 1, 2019
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
Subject to the safety requirements of a bicycle, and its rider has a bicycle rider's rights and duties, including the duty of due care
Like a bicycle, may treat a stop sign as a yield sign: slow down, yield, then proceed without stopping
On a sidewalk or crosswalk, the rider must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing
May be ridden wherever bicycles may, including multi-use paths, unless excluded by local ordinance or by signs the agency in charge posts after putting the exclusion on its board's agenda
Not subject to driver's license, title, registration, plate or financial responsibility requirements
A violation by its rider of the rules of the road is an infraction
